items.title: Louis Keppard Interview, 1961-01-19
items.q: George Barquet. Yeah, I played with him.

ctx.x: Do you remember George Barquet, the one that played with your brother? Can you tell us anything much about him? Do you remember George?

George Barquet. Yeah, I played with him. George was a good clarinet player, too. And he is a player of funerals. And he was a funer man. He didn't miss a lick. He was right there on the job. Well, I tell you, if I am mistaken, I believe he was a better musician. Not in the line of musician, but in the line of playing, I believe he was better than Alphonse Piku. In a funeral. Because he used to play some tough music, and he used to make that clarinet cry like a baby. He was solid. He was good. Of course, Piku is…
That's what I've heard other people, too, and told me that, too.
